subject: GCP listing enablement: procurement intake & billing mapping
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: GCP Partner Desk <gcp-partner@google.com>; Julia Martin <julia.martin@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: GCP listing enablement: procurement intake & billing mapping

Hi team,

Thanks for taking time on the call earlier. Acme is ready to move forward with a GCP Marketplace listing but procurement has asked for a clear billing path and a mapped intake document so they can route purchase orders correctly. I attached the GCP billing mapping template and our internal listing checklist for context.

Can GCP confirm the recommended Marketplace SKU structure (monthly vs. annual) and whether marketplace billing will appear on Acme's invoice as a Google line item or as a partner-managed invoice? Julia from Acme is looped in — she can share procurement constraints (PO windows, PO numbering, and taxese) if helpful.

Next steps I propose:
- GCP: confirm billing display and recommended SKU granularity
- Acme: share procurement contact + any mandatory fields for PO processing
- Redwood: prepare a procurement intake doc with example fields that Acme can drop into their SOW

Attached: gcp-billing-mapping-template.xlsx (attachment), redwood-gcp-listing-checklist.pdf (attachment).

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Lead, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: GCP Partner Desk <gcp-partner@google.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Julia Martin <julia.martin@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 13:04:21 -0800
Subject: Re: GCP listing enablement: procurement intake & billing mapping

Hi Karthik — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick answers to your bullets: 

- Billing display: Marketplace charges will appear on the customer's Google invoice as a Google line item if Acme purchases directly through the GCP Marketplace subscription. If Acme requests partner-managed invoicing, we can enable Partner Billing but it requires additional commerce onboarding and an annual commitment.
- SKU granularity: We recommend SKU per billing cadence (monthly vs annual) and a separate SKU for support/add-ons to simplify PO line-item matching.

Julia — from a procurement perspective, please confirm whether Acme requires a separate billing contact, PO number format (prefix), and whether tax-exempt certificates are needed. If you can share examples of a typical PO, that will speed internal approvals.

I’ve created a Partner Portal ticket to track commerce onboarding: https://partners.cloud.google.com/support/ticket/PP-45231

Regards,
GCP Partner Desk
GCP Marketplace Enablement
From: Julia Martin <julia.martin@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, GCP Partner Desk <gcp-partner@google.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 08:12:03 -0800
Subject: Re: GCP listing enablement: procurement intake & billing mapping

Thanks — attaching a sanitized example PO that our procurement team uses. Key notes:
- PO numbers use prefix ACME-PO-YYYY-#### (please include the ACME-PO field in any billing metadata)
- We require a billing contact name, email, and a remit-to address for wire instructions
- For SaaS purchases under $100k annual we can accept Google invoice line items; for purchases above that threshold procurement prefers partner billing and consolidated invoicing

Attaching: acme-sample-po.pdf (external attachment).

Julia Martin
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 11:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: GCP listing enablement: procurement intake & billing mapping

Karthik / Jonas —

I drafted a procurement intake form tailored to Acme based on Julia's PO notes and the GCP template. Main changes: added an "ACME_PO_NUMBER" field to line up to their prefix requirement, a boolean for "partner_managed_billing" and a remit-to block for wire info. I also added guidance on SKU naming (SKU_MONTHLY: redwood-inference-standard-monthly, SKU_ANNUAL: redwood-inference-standard-annual) and a recommended clause for support add-ons.

I attached the draft intake as an XLSX and the checklist we should run before requesting partner billing. Would like Jonas to confirm whether these SKUs align with our pricing matrix and whether we need legal to pre-approve the partner-managed billing T&Cs before we request onboarding.

Marissa
Senior Partner Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: GCP Partner Desk <gcp-partner@google.com>, Julia Martin <julia.martin@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GCP listing enablement: procurement intake & billing mapping

Thanks everyone — action items and owners below: 

1) GCP Partner Desk: Please confirm whether partner-managed billing onboarding can be completed within 3 weeks if Acme elects that path (ticket PP-45231).
2) Acme / Julia: Confirm whether purchase will be under $100k or above (this will decide billing path).
3) Marissa: finalize the procurement intake XLSX and include the ACME_PO_NUMBER field; tag Lauren for legal review on partner billing terms.
4) Jonas: validate SKU names vs pricing matrix; note any differences and call out if we need adjusted unit prices for marketplace SKUs.

I’ll schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to lock down the decision and kick off commerce onboarding if needed. Tentative meeting invite to follow.

Best,
Karthik
